title: Use strict BM25 lexical retrieval in v1
answer: V1 is strictly BM25 lexical search. Hybrid retrieval is a future direction; do not describe v1 as semantic search.

title: Support three coding-agent session sources
answer: Support Codex, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot CLI sessions. Actual formats and project metadata must be verified.

title: Restrict v1 session search to the current project
answer: Search only sessions associated with the current project. Cross-project search is deferred.

title: Refresh automatically and honor gitignore
answer: Refresh project and session indexes automatically as agents work and files change. Project indexing honors .gitignore to exclude unwanted files.

title: Index while MCP clients are active
answer: Indexing runs while at least one MCP client is active, stops after the last disconnect, and reconciles offline changes on reconnect. The ownership mechanism remains to be designed.

title: Search messages and tool activity
answer: Index conversation messages, tool calls, and tool outputs. Return bounded excerpts with session identity and timestamps, with surrounding context available on demand. The context retrieval contract remains open.

title: Share session history across worktrees
answer: Worktrees of the same repository share searchable session history. Each worktree has its own code index.
basis: User accepted shared session history recommendation

title: Return source passages with locations
answer: Search source code and project documentation. Return relevant passages with paths, line ranges, and bounded snippets; group nearby matches to reduce repetition.

title: Expose separate project and session search tools
answer: Expose search_project and search_sessions as separate search tools.

title: Automatically discover session history
answer: Automatically discover supported agents' local session history and import sessions associated with the repository, then follow updates. Optional location overrides are proposed; do not associate sessions with a project when ownership cannot be established.
basis: User chose automatic discovery; overrides and unknown-ownership exclusion are planning recommendations

title: Serve search during initial indexing
answer: Serve results as indexing progresses and report building, ready, or error state so incomplete coverage is visible.

title: Persist indexes locally
answer: Persist local indexes across disconnects. Reconcile changed and deleted source content on reconnect; preserve cache when indexing stops.
basis: User accepted persistent local index recommendation

title: Require macOS and Windows
answer: MacOS and Windows are required for v1. Linux is optional if the same implementation supports it without substantial extra work.

title: Build from source and launch with a command

title: Use client-launched stdio frontends and one repository owner
recommendation: Each MCP client launches a lightweight stdio frontend. Frontends for the same Git common directory attach to one local owner process. The owner manages shared session history and separate code indexes for active worktrees.
rationale: Client subprocess lifetime provides a concrete connection signal.
One owner prevents duplicate session indexing and competing writes across worktrees.
No always-on service or manual server startup is required.

alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler startup, but duplicate parsing/indexing and competing cache ownership.

alternatives.option: One manually launched Streamable HTTP server
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses more existing transport code, but manual lifecycle and HTTP session expiration fit active-client indexing less directly.

lifecycle: An OS-backed exclusive owner lock arbitrates startup; do not use a PID alone as proof of ownership.
An authenticated local connection registers each frontend and its worktree; IPC mechanism remains to be selected for macOS and Windows.
Frontend exits on MCP stdin closure and closes its owner connection. Owner detects closed connections; bounded health checking covers hung peers.
Code watching runs only for worktrees with attached clients; session indexing runs while any repository client is attached.
Last disconnect cancels new indexing work; finish or abandon a safe publication boundary, persist state, and exit.
Owner crash requires election/reconnect and source reconciliation. Concurrent arrival during shutdown must retry attachment, not create a second writer.
identity: Resolve Git common directory for repository grouping and worktree root for code scope. Separate clones are not merged merely because remotes match. Unknown or removed worktree attribution remains a compatibility investigation.
validation_status: Design analysis only; multi-process lifecycle and Windows behavior untested.

title: Publish immutable BM25 generations with matching metadata
recommendation: Use application-owned normalized text/tokens and metadata, build immutable BM25 snapshots, and publish coherent generations. Evaluate SQLite for source state, chunk metadata, parser offsets, and the active-generation pointer. Avoid the current BM25 WAL.
publication_contract: Capture a bounded input revision and assign generation-local BM25 document IDs mapped to stable source/chunk identities.
Write each candidate snapshot to a unique immutable generation filename; never overwrite a snapshot still used by queries.
Validate the candidate snapshot and matching metadata, then commit the active generation and its source offsets together in the metadata store.
Swap the in-memory index and metadata as one shared generation. Each query pins one generation for its full duration.
Restart validates active snapshot presence and checksum; missing or invalid snapshots trigger fallback/rebuild and incomplete-coverage status, never mixed metadata.
Reclaim old snapshots only after no query uses them; retry deferred cleanup where Windows file handles prevent deletion.
important_limit: A SQLite commit does not atomically commit external snapshot files. Publication ordering, file and directory durability, retained generations, and restart validation are separate required contracts.
update_strategy: Debounce changes and rebuild the affected logical collection initially as a benchmark candidate. Do not claim this meets freshness targets until measured. Segmentation or WAL repair is conditional on that measurement.
ranking_constraint: Independent shard scores are not globally comparable without a defined corpus-statistics strategy. Do not silently merge per-file BM25 scores as if they were one corpus.

alternatives.tradeoff: Potentially cheaper updates, but confirmed scoring, tokenizer, identity, and recovery defects increase correctness work.
Smaller rebuild units, but naive score merging changes ranking semantics.

validation_status: Proposed design; publication protocol and workload cost untested.

recommendation: Immediate responses from the latest complete index, with explicit freshness/backlog status and a target of a few seconds for ordinary edits, subject to measurement.
tradeoff: Waiting after edits improves freshness but adds variable latency and needs a precise capture boundary because files can change while a query runs.

title: Raw term postings permit differential edits with current BM25 statistics
method: Retain per-chunk raw term frequencies and document lengths; replace/delete only the changed chunk postings, update document count, total token count and term document frequencies, then score query matches using existing bm25_turbo::scoring functions. Compare document identities and scores against a fresh BM25Builder index after each update.
limits: Small synthetic corpus only
No throughput or memory conclusions
Probe is mutable and single-threaded, with no durable storage
Does not validate identifier tokenization, actual chunking, or every BM25 variant
implication: Reusing scoring kernels is viable even if the precomputed score matrix is not the best live index representation.

title: Treat working-tree files as truth and Git metadata as change hints
algorithm: Ordinary saves: debounce events per path, read a stable file version, hash content, and skip unchanged bytes. Reparse changed files and diff chunk identities rather than reindexing the whole repository.
Fetch without working-tree changes: do not rebuild code indexes merely because remote refs or object storage changed. Downloads into the worktree follow ordinary file discovery and ignore rules.

Checkout/pull/reset: build candidate paths from old-to-new HEAD changes, watcher events, previously dirty paths, and current dirty/untracked paths. Previous dirty paths matter when a switch cleans a path.
Reconcile file membership after reconnect, watcher overflow, ignore-rule changes, or incomplete Git metadata. Missing sources invalidate old chunks.
Cache normalized chunks and term frequencies by content hash plus parser/tokenizer version. Retain source identity separately, so equal content at different paths stays distinguishable.
Revisiting a branch can reuse content-derived artifacts, but a branch name or commit alone cannot identify the active index when dirty/untracked files or ignore settings differ.
Pin source revision and chunk-location metadata together. Detect HEAD/index changes during reconciliation and schedule another pass; do not claim checkout completion from one filesystem event.
local_evidence: Ten adjacent commit comparisons in t3code touched 1 to 10 files each, 45 file-change entries in total. This is a small sample, not a branch-switch benchmark.
limitations: No live branch switching or downloads performed
Only one worktree in each inspected repository
Windows and removed worktrees remain untested
Adjacent history entries are revision-pair comparisons, not guaranteed single-parent commit deltas.

title: Compare live raw postings with cached full snapshot rebuilds
preferred_candidate: Immutable base posting segments plus small changed-chunk deltas, tombstones, current corpus statistics, and generation-local active-version lookup. Evaluate a simpler mutable owner plus immutable published views before implementing segment machinery.
reuse: Reuse BM25 scoring kernels, tokenizer components where suitable, selection helpers and MCP scaffolding. This changes the live storage representation; it does not replace lexical retrieval with another model.
consistency: Only the active version of each source chunk contributes to postings or corpus statistics.
Publish postings, active-version mapping, statistics and source locations coherently.
Query scoring uses one set of current corpus statistics for all segments. Never merge independently normalized segment BM25 scores.
Compaction changes representation only; identities and scores must remain equivalent.

alternatives.option: Cache parsing/tokenization, then rebuild the full precomputed matrix
alternatives.tradeoff: Maximum direct engine reuse and simpler reads, but corpus-wide scoring work remains after each batch.

alternatives.option: Base precomputed scores plus separately scored delta
alternatives.tradeoff: Quick to assemble, but incompatible score statistics can distort ranking; not recommended without a proven correction method.

next_evidence: Benchmark cached full rebuilds and raw-posting updates on representative project/session corpora, measuring refresh latency, query latency, memory, and branch-return cache benefit. Do not select thresholds before measurements.

title: SQLite transactions provide consistent synthetic chunk generations during concurrent reads
limits: No power-loss test
No Windows test
No real source text
SQL snapshot checks are not search latency measurements
In-memory posting publication cost remains unmeasured
SQLite 3.51.0 is the local probe runtime; production must use a WAL-reset-fixed release. Only one connection writes/checkpoints during this probe.
interpretation: Supports SQLite as authoritative transactional storage for normalized chunks, offsets, statistics and generation identity. Does not validate in-memory BM25 posting publication or end-to-end freshness. Do not add these synthetic timings to prior benchmark timings as an end-to-end measurement.
dependency_gate: Use SQLite 3.51.3 or later, or a documented fixed backport, for production. Local 3.51.0 probe used one writer/checkpointer connection and reader-only connections; its success is not evidence that the documented WAL-reset race is fixed.

title: Keep authoritative differential state in one transactional store
recommendation: Store normalized chunk records, source identity/version, parser offsets, raw term counts, corpus statistics and generation identity in one local SQLite database per repository owner. Treat in-memory postings and optional snapshot files as rebuildable derived state.
publication_contract: Prepare an update against a known source/input generation.
Commit matching source/chunk/statistics/offset changes together. Do not expose half-committed state.
Publish a matching immutable or versioned search view only after commit; responses report the published generation and pending refresh state.
If the process stops after commit but before publication, rebuild/replay the derived search view from committed state.
If publication allocation fails, keep serving the previous coherent view with incomplete/freshness status and retry; do not declare the new generation published.
Apply verified-current source filtering independently of snapshot consistency so coherent old-branch data is not presented as current.
alternatives: Serve term postings directly from SQLite read transactions, trading query I/O for lower memory and simpler generation consistency.
Maintain persistent immutable posting structures or base-plus-delta views, trading more implementation work for faster queries and bounded copying.

title: Numeric term IDs substantially reduce code-index memory
method: Stream eligible chunks into one raw-postings index, without retaining the whole token corpus or building the precomputed comparison index. Compare string-keyed per-document hash maps against interned numeric term IDs and contiguous per-document/per-term frequency vectors.
validation: Numeric vector query path matched a fresh BM25 build on three small synthetic queries. Actual repository run measured peak RSS only, not full result equivalence.

Source text cache, sessions, concurrent publication, and persistent-store cache excluded
512 MiB aggregate target remains unproven
recommendation: Use interned numeric term IDs and compact posting storage as the next design candidate. Budget base, mutable deltas, query working memory and shared session history together; avoid whole-index cloning during updates.

Use watchers plus reconciliation for plain folders; Git change hints are optional accelerators.

title: bm25-mcp v1 implementation specification

architecture.search: Independent project-code and repository-session BM25 collections; raw postings use shared live corpus statistics within each collection. No embeddings or independent-segment score fusion.
architecture.ownership: Recommended: one repository-family owner shared by client-launched stdio frontends; worktree code collections activate only while clients for those worktrees exist. Plain folders use canonical configured-root identity. Transport and owner election remain detailed-design work.
architecture.durability: Recommended: SQLite is the authoritative transactional store for normalized chunk state, source versions, parser offsets, statistics and generation identity. In-memory search views are derived and recoverable.
architecture.publication: Prepare candidate changes without mutating pinned reader views; commit authoritative changes; publish one matching search generation. An interrupted publication recovers from committed state. Never mix postings, statistics or source metadata from different generations.
architecture.memory: Use numeric term IDs and compact arrays with shared immutable data, bounded pending deltas and bounded caches. Count code collections, session collection, active queries, pending generations and database caches toward the 512 MiB soft target. Prevent unbounded old-generation retention.
architecture.change_discovery: Use filesystem events as hints and reconciliation as the correctness backstop. Hash actual worktree bytes; Git changes narrow candidate paths but do not replace dirty/untracked file handling. Fetch-only ref changes do not force reindexing.
architecture.eligibility: Strictly apply ignore rules even to tracked files; reject binary content before tokenization. Changes in eligibility invalidate prior chunks. Benchmark file-size caps are not adopted as product policy.
architecture.sessions: Provider-specific adapters normalize messages and tool events, retain provenance, correlate results, avoid duplicate Codex streams, and exclude this MCP result bodies. Tail complete records and retain safe parser offsets; tolerate interrupted calls. Unknown project ownership stays excluded.
architecture.freshness: Serve immediate results from an available coherent generation. During transitions return only passages verified against current sources and report partial coverage. Do not claim a generation is exactly a Git commit solely from HEAD observations.

title: Use per-client stdio frontends and a leased repository owner
basis: Agent technical design within accepted active-client, multi-worktree and cross-platform requirements

answer.launch: One source-built binary exposes a foreground stdio MCP command and an internal owner mode. The configured project root is fixed for each frontend connection.
answer.identity: Repository owner key derives from canonical Git common-directory identity; plain-folder owner key derives from canonical configured root. Worktree roots identify separate code collections.
answer.ipc: Use a loopback-only local TCP connection between frontend and owner, authenticated with an owner-instance random capability stored in a user-private runtime directory. This is internal IPC, not a remotely accessible MCP HTTP endpoint.
answer.election: Hold an OS-backed exclusive lock on a persistent per-owner lock file for the owner lifetime. Do not delete/recreate the lock inode or use PID alone for election. Publish protocol version, instance nonce and endpoint only after listening.
answer.attachment: Frontends attach to a compatible live owner; on refused connection or stale endpoint, retry election under the lock. Reject incompatible protocol versions with a actionable error rather than sharing an incompatible database.
answer.lifetime: Count registered frontend connections, with liveness probes for unresponsive peers. A stdio EOF or lost owner connection releases the lease. After no live leases are known, stop new indexing, safely finish or abandon the current publication boundary, then exit. Detection latency is explicit; no always-on service is installed.
answer.worktrees: Only attached worktrees need active code watchers. Shared session indexing remains active while any repository frontend lease exists.
answer.shutdown_race: A frontend arriving during shutdown retries attachment/election. Single ownership is enforced by the lock, not endpoint-file timing.
answer.failure: Owner crash releases the lock; frontend reconnects, owner recovers committed state and reconciles sources. Never terminate an unrelated process based on a cached PID.

title: Use SQLite authoritative state and immutable search generations
basis: Agent technical design supported by selected raw-postings architecture and bounded transaction/publication probes

answer.authority: One local SQLite database per owner stores source versions, immutable chunk versions/text, active chunk membership, stable numeric term IDs, raw term counts, corpus statistics, safe parser offsets, schema/tokenizer versions and committed generation identity.
answer.transactions: A writer transaction commits affected membership, statistics and source/parser state together. A failed transaction leaves the previous generation authoritative. New term IDs are committed with the chunks that use them.
answer.publication: Prepare replacement immutable posting vectors and source-metadata handles while old readers continue. Commit durable state, then publish one matching shared generation pointer. A failure between commit and publication leaves an older served generation marked behind and is recoverable from committed state.
answer.source_text: Fetch excerpts lazily using immutable chunk-version keys pinned by the query generation. Never resolve an old posting against newly overwritten source-location metadata.
answer.retention: Track references to query generations; reclaim unreferenced immutable versions and cache entries under a bounded policy. Do not let idle cursors pin memory generations indefinitely. Cache retention never substitutes for source-session retention policy.
answer.recovery: SQLite is authoritative; rebuild derived views or replay committed changes from a validated checkpoint. Optional snapshot files are derived caches, not a second source of truth.
answer.sqlite: Use a release with the documented WAL-reset fix; single-writer ownership and explicit checkpoint policy. Keep the cache on a local filesystem with appropriate per-user permissions.
answer.memory: Account for vocabulary, base postings, deltas, source metadata, query accumulators, database cache and concurrently pinned generations. Avoid full index duplication per client or update.

title: Stream all eligible text without a default file-size cutoff
answer: Stream all nonignored, non-binary text in bounded chunks by default. Offer explicit configurable exclusions and optional size limits; do not adopt the benchmark-only 2 MiB file cutoff. Report progress and incomplete coverage for long-running large-file indexing.
constraints: Bound decoder, line, token and chunk buffers; a single huge line must not require loading the entire file.

Session JSONL requires bounded or streaming handling of oversized individual records, not merely reading one unbounded line at a time. Existing extractors are probes, not the production ingestion contract.
Do not silently truncate text to meet memory targets; report explicitly configured exclusions or parsing failures.
Separate large-file and bulk-change convergence from the accepted ordinary-edit freshness workload.
If a source changes during reading, do not mark an inconsistent read complete. Retry/reconcile and retain explicit partial status.

title: Bounded ingestion, source verification and memory pressure

source_verification.rule: Mark affected sources unknown/ineligible immediately when changes or reconciliation invalidate confidence. Return only eligible passages; suppress unverified candidates and report partial coverage instead of rehashing large files on the query path.
source_verification.reconcile: On reconnect, watcher overflow, unknown state or ambiguous branch transition, invalidate relevant source confidence until asynchronous stable-byte checks complete. Git narrows candidate work but Git blob IDs, clean status, size and mtime alone do not prove current working-tree bytes.
source_verification.hashing: Stream a content digest while staging source chunks; inspect file identity and metadata before and after reads and retry unstable reads. Preserve verification time and observed source version.
source_verification.query: Pin index/provenance generation and check current eligibility before returning excerpts. Apply bounded candidate verification work; report incomplete coverage rather than blocking for bulk reconciliation.
source_verification.limit: Verification describes the source version observed at verification time. It does not promise an atomic repository snapshot or prevent a file changing after verification.

text_processing.encoding: Accept valid UTF-8, UTF-8 BOM and BOM-marked UTF-16 LE/BE with incremental decoders. Report unsupported encodings separately from binary exclusions; never silently replace malformed bytes.
text_processing.chunks: Bound decoded chunk bodies to 16 KiB UTF-8, preferring line/blank-line boundaries and approximately 60 lines. Split a giant line on UTF-8 boundaries; preserve line number plus byte/column segment offsets for every piece. Chunk sizes are processing units, not content cutoffs.
text_processing.tokenization: Use identical versioned document/query normalization, retaining case-folded identifier forms plus camelCase/snake_case components, with no stemming or stopword deletion in v1. Deduplicate equivalent emitted forms at each lexical occurrence. Store only numeric term IDs in hot postings.
text_processing.oversized_tokens: Do not buffer unbounded tokens. Normalize incrementally; exceptionally long tokens use a domain-separated digest term instead of retaining their entire spelling in the vocabulary. Apply the same deterministic rule to queries and preserve complete source text in bounded stored chunks. Validate this rule independently of the existing default-tokenizer probes.
text_processing.session_records: Use incremental JSON structure/string decoding or disk spooling with bounded decoding, including strings within a single oversized JSONL record. Do not reject a valid record solely because it exceeds the benchmark chunk size. Malformed or unsupported records yield explicit degraded coverage and safe resynchronization; do not silently truncate.
text_processing.offsets: Advance durable session parse offsets only with committed normalized chunks, after a complete valid record. Keep incomplete tails pending and reconcile replacement/truncation.

pressure.target: 512 MiB per owner across all active worktrees, shared sessions, metadata, queries, database caches and unpublished generations; this remains a soft target.
order: Bound ingestion queues and decoding buffers; apply backpressure.
Evict recomputable source/token caches and unpinned old generations.
Throttle background builds and coalesce superseded updates rather than accumulating them.
Use disk-resident authoritative posting rows and bounded hot caches when a whole collection cannot fit; exact BM25 statistics and source filtering must remain consistent across memory and disk paths.
Report memory pressure, slowed convergence and any target breach explicitly. Never silently omit eligible sources to claim the memory target is met.
pressure.validation: Measure disk-backed query latency and commit/publication overhead before acceptance; this path has not been benchmarked.

dependency_and_build.rust_version: Choose an explicit minimum supported Rust version compatible with selected cross-platform locking APIs; raise the new project minimum if needed rather than relying on unavailable Rust 1.85 APIs.
dependency_and_build.dependencies: Resolve and lock dependency versions during bootstrap; use the documented SQLite WAL-reset fix requirement. Existing source licensing notices must be preserved.

sections.Problem Statement: Coding agents need fast local retrieval of relevant project passages and previous work across Codex, Claude Code and Copilot CLI. Repeated scans and disconnected histories lose context; edits and branch switches can make stored results misleading.
sections.Solution: A source-built local MCP server provides strict BM25 lexical project search and project-scoped session search. It discovers histories automatically, persists indexes locally, refreshes while clients are connected, and immediately returns verified results with explicit freshness and coverage. The architecture permits later hybrid retrieval without adding semantic search to v1.
User Stories: Start the server against a Git worktree or ordinary folder and search relevant text through search_project.
Find paths, line ranges and bounded source excerpts with filters and explicit freshness while indexing continues.
Edit, rename, delete, download or switch branches and have eligible search content reconcile automatically.
Keep ignored files and binary content out of results, including tracked files covered by ignore rules.
Search automatically discovered Codex, Claude Code and Copilot CLI conversations and supported tool activity for this project.
Expand a session match into bounded, version-safe surrounding context through search_sessions.
Share session history across worktrees of one repository while searching each worktree code separately.
Attach multiple MCP clients without duplicating repository indexes; stop indexing when the final client disconnects.
Reconnect after offline changes or an owner crash and recover durable state with honest coverage during reconciliation.
Index large valid text and large JSONL events without silent content loss, with bounded processing and visible memory pressure.
Build and launch from source on macOS and Windows.
Implementation Decisions: Expose exactly search_project and search_sessions. Bind a connection to its configured root. Plain lexical query text has an 8192-byte UTF-8 maximum, rejected rather than truncated. Return structuredContent and equivalent JSON TextContent with declared schemas.

Project search accepts query, relative path_glob, limit (default 10, maximum 50), and max_response_bytes (default 16384, maximum 65536). Filter before top-k, group overlapping excerpts and preserve scores. Matches carry stable identity, relative path, line range, excerpt, score and source version.

Session search accepts query, agent/session/date filters and the same limits. UTC date bounds are inclusive after and exclusive before; missing timestamps are explicit and excluded by time filters. Context mode on the same tool accepts match_id, before/after event counts (default 2, maximum 10 each), budget and optional cursor. Source-changed or expired IDs return explicit errors. Context is normalized verbatim source with provenance; cursors do not pin RAM indefinitely.

Every response exposes building/ready/refreshing/degraded, generation, reconciled time, pending changes or unknown, exclusion/error counts and truncation/continuation. Distinguish no published generation from a successful search with no matches. Reject invalid argument combinations.

Use compact raw term-frequency postings with numeric term IDs and current corpus statistics in immutable shared generations. Reuse pinned, attributed BM25 Turbo scoring, selection and suitable tokenizer/MCP code. Use a fresh BM25Builder as correctness oracle; do not reuse the defective WAL unchanged.

SQLite is authoritative for source/chunk versions and text, membership, term IDs/counts, corpus statistics, parser offsets and schema/tokenizer/generation versions. Commit atomically before publishing a matching search generation. Pin immutable excerpt keys with each query; recover derived views from durable state. Require a SQLite release carrying the WAL-reset fix and a defined migration/rebuild policy.

One owner serves a Git repository family or canonical plain root. Per-client stdio frontends use authenticated loopback TCP with private capability storage, compatible protocol checks and an OS lifetime exclusive lock on a persistent lock file. Handle simultaneous startup, stale endpoints, crash recovery and shutdown/attach races. Active worktrees have separate code collections; sessions are shared. Last lease loss stops new indexing and exits at a safe publication boundary; liveness latency is explicit.

Watcher events and Git metadata guide differential work. Invalidate uncertain source eligibility immediately; asynchronously read stable bytes and hash content. Git object IDs, status, size and mtime alone do not prove working-tree currency. Queries return only verified-current passages and never hash huge sources synchronously. Verification describes observed source state, not an atomic filesystem snapshot.

Honor strict Git ignore eligibility even for tracked files; classify binary by content. Incrementally decode UTF-8, UTF-8 BOM and BOM-marked UTF-16 LE/BE; report unsupported encodings separately without lossy replacement. No default file-size cap. Optional user exclusions/caps must be visible in coverage.

Use 16 KiB UTF-8 chunks, preferring line/blank boundaries and approximately 60 lines. Split giant lines with precise segment offsets. Version identical query/document normalization: case-folded whole identifiers plus camel/snake components, deduplicated per occurrence, without stemming or stopwords. Normalize huge tokens incrementally into domain-separated digest terms under the same query rule.

Discover provider histories under CODEX_HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and COPILOT_HOME with the agreed user-home defaults and explicit overrides. Normalize visible user/assistant text and supported tool calls/results, excluding reasoning, system bookkeeping and opaque binary fields. Deduplicate Codex event streams; pair Claude tool blocks and Copilot start/completion variants. Record source identity, offsets, provider/schema versions and unknown-type diagnostics.

Bound JSONL decoding using incremental parsing or disk spooling even inside huge strings. Only commit parse offsets with complete records and corresponding chunks. Leave incomplete tails pending, reconcile rewrites/truncation/deletion and preserve unfinished tool calls. Exclude own search-result bodies using exact provider-mapped identity while retaining calls and surrounding conversation; do not suppress same-named unrelated tools.

Associate sessions from verified cwd/root evidence. Persist known worktree associations; never guess from names/remotes. More-specific registered plain roots win. Attribute cwd-changing events where boundaries are known; exclude ambiguous portions visibly. Source deletion removes active membership; this is not an archive.

Target 512 MiB soft owner RSS across worktrees, sessions, queries, caches and concurrent generations. Bound queues, evict derivable data, coalesce updates and throttle ingestion; use disk-resident authoritative postings with bounded hot caches when needed. Preserve exact statistics and coverage; report pressure or breaches instead of silently omitting content.

Provide an independent Rust source build and foreground serve command with an explicit minimum Rust version, locked dependencies and preserved upstream attribution. macOS and Windows are required; Linux is optional when inexpensive.
Testing Decisions: Test search ranking against fresh-build BM25 after insertion, replacement, deletion and compaction with production normalization. Existing upstream count-only compaction checks are insufficient; score and identity equivalence are required.

Test ingestion and reconciliation with strict tracked-ignore exclusion, binary replacement, huge lines/tokens, supported encodings, unstable reads, renames, watcher overflow, offline edits and disposable Git checkout transitions.

Test durable publication with real index queries across concurrent pinned generations, restart, interrupted transactions and commit-before-publication failure. Ensure excerpts and provenance always correspond to the pinned generation.

Test every provider with sanitized schema fixtures covering duplicate streams, tool pairing, unknown types, timestamp gaps, cwd changes, incomplete/huge/malformed records, rewrites and own-result exclusion. Use real project histories for smoke checks without logging their content.

Test both tools over MCP including filters before top-k, budgets, no-match versus not-ready, invalid arguments, context expiry and continuation. Check separate worktree code, shared repository sessions and unrelated-root isolation.
Test owner election, attachment, disconnect, process-tree behavior, protocol mismatch, stale endpoints and crash recovery on macOS and Windows.

Measure at least 1000 warm end-to-end MCP queries for single/four clients with a p95 target below 100 ms. Target ordinary edits becoming searchable within 2 seconds of stable write for 1/10-file batches up to 1 MiB changed text. This workload definition is not an input cap. Use the small BM25 repository, larger t3code corpus, session-heavy neutron corpus and sanitized Claude fixtures. Measure complete owner peak RSS during updates and readers, including disk-backed retrieval. Record expected-source relevance checks and actual top-k judgments separately from score equivalence.

Existing raw-postings, compact-generation and SQLite probes support feasibility, but used bounded workloads and tested components separately. They do not establish product latency, complete memory use, production tokenizer correctness or Windows support. Prepare a reproducible PowerShell handoff; user performs actual Windows validation.
